CS5-01.note: The colon is an explicit gloss: 'a residue of manufacture with no bearing on how the sheet aged' = incidental. B is the finding the curators missed, C and D are off-axis. Well built but the appositive hands over the answer; this is a module-1 difficulty.

CS5-02.note: 'males recorded forty years apart shared the same terminal trill' fixes invariant. Difficulty comes from vocabulary register (stochastic/attenuated/polymorphic), not from reasoning; the since-clause supplies the answer before the complication arrives.

CS5-03.note: Best item of the completion group. B (flakes badly) and D (recipe copied wholesale) are both literally asserted, so a solver who stops at sentence two picks one of them; only 'uninformative' is what the isotope finding overturns and what makes the discarded barrows painful. Two stated traps and one inferential key.

CS5-04.note: Double inversion: 'one hand working once and at leisure' = written up afterwards, so the assumption UV kills is retrospective, and the evidence (ink changing at port calls, later days filling margins earlier days left) shows contemporaneity. B is the trap for solvers who match the evidence to the blank instead of to the refuted assumption. Last sentence correctly fences off A.

CS5-05.note: Disagree with the author's self-report. 'neither is the quicker to work with: the same synchronisms must be checked either way' is an explicit kill on Efficiency, and the last sentence defines parsimony outright. The senses are disjoint in the frame the passage builds; the cost is that the pre-emption lowers difficulty, not that two options survive.

CS5-06.note: The one genuinely contestable key in the batch. Subject is 'the diarist's account', a thing that shows rather than a mind that admits, and 'register' in the show/betray sense (a face registers surprise) is directly supported by the flat syntax and by 'Grief enters the diary only four months later' — an entry-into-the-text framing. I pick Acknowledge because she does indicate the facts of the loss (mill wall, bridge, sheep), so what is absent is recognition of the loss AS loss; but D survives on the passage as written and a careful solver can defend it. Fix by changing the subject to the diarist, or by adding a clause that rules out the display sense.

CS5-07.passage_needed_reason: 'the question ... was settled' defaults to Concluded from the stem alone, and the key is that default. C (Discharged) collocates with debts and duties, not questions, so it is eliminable from the stem with no passage at all.
CS5-07.note: Agree with the author and it is worse than described. A is killed by the first clause and C by collocation, leaving B against a weak D, with B also the blind default. Re-key or re-write so a non-default sense is correct — as written this is a free item.

CS5-08.note: 'It is not spare' pre-empts A explicitly, and the substitution appendix plus 'a report nobody outside the field can read is not a report' fixes Accessible. B has no candor evidence. Clean; the explicit pre-emption keeps it at medium rather than hard.

CS5-09.note: Full 2x2 minimal pair (which surface, which direction). Boulders lie flat, hold snow six weeks longer, so less growing season and thalli smaller than their age implies — which is why the 1710 date is too young. A is the direction trap, B/C the surface trap. Nothing is reachable by option shape.

CS5-10.note: The evidence the rest of the text actually supplies is the fee paid and the unissued masters. B is the near miss: the denied royalty is in sentence one (the setup), not in what tests the reading, and 'a week's wage' is only the yardstick. A and C are fabrications. Two-option endgame, so medium rather than easy.

CS5-11.note: The sentence states both halves — tended rows survive and stay small, closed stands keep shrinking. D invents a minimum detection height and B requires the rows to be adding canopy that offsets losses, which the sentence denies. Sound.

CS5-12.note: Two reasons, both in the last sentence: the terms predate the change, and the form itself was revised in 1806. A is the sharpest distractor but the form revision dates nothing, so 'two reasons' fails for it. C and D overreach.

CS5-13.note: Last sentence is plainly a cost (biomass to clear, funding per cut). A inverts its valence, B describes sentence one, D invents a dispute. Straight structure item, no second pass needed.

CS5-14.note: Agree with the author and worse than described: TWO options are rejectable, not one. A is incoherent on its face (explaining a non-clustered western pattern by raiding recorded in the east) and C contradicts the final clause outright. That leaves the stock null option B against D. Easiest structure item in the batch.

CS5-15.note: 'only by a fifth of the gap' and 'the remainder tracks the concentration of a small solute' are both verbatim, so the item reduces to number matching. D is incoherent (temperature is the condition, not a competing cause). No inference above paraphrase.

CS5-16.note: Agree with the author and worse than described. A is eliminable on option shape alone — three options open 'help readers', one opens 'cost the psalm' — and B (several speakers) and C (couplet answering) have no foothold anywhere in the text, while the key paraphrases 'agree with one another far less often' directly. Free item once the shape split is noticed.

CS5-17.note: A is a good trap: the overnight park agreement is in the passage, but it is the control that validates the sensors, not the comparison the text exists to report. B and C are outside the text. The trap being an in-passage detail rather than an invention is what keeps this above easy.

CS5-18.note: The rite reserves a job no other instrument can do, and the fiddlers come home to it. D is the nearest miss and misreads the causal direction — they came home FOR the wedding months, not because travel was impossible then. B and C are unsupported. The isolation premise is set up and refuted cleanly.

CS5-19.note: The inversion holds: the field's stock answer (actigraphy scores stillness as sleep) is named in Text 2's first sentence but nothing in Text 2 supports the misclassification claim, which has to be imported. The door confound is evidenced three ways (co-timing, dose-response with corridor brightness, null on the ward already re-doored). C and D are unstated, and Text 2 closes staffing off explicitly. Note the actigraphy clause is load-free otherwise — it exists only as the trap, which a suspicious solver may read as a tell.

CS5-20.note: Disagree with the author's flag. A (legume nitrogen) is the stock answer and is explicitly neutralised by the common soil-nitrogen target, C by equal weed counts; the sowing-date confound is the only live one and is quantified (wet autumns in eight of ten years). D is unsupported but not rejectable without reading, so 'one rejectable option' overstates it. Best of the four the author flagged; leave it alone.

CS5-21.note: Counting method changed with the charge, and the household surveys show no real change — both stated. B, C, D are all outside Text 2. Clean but transparent.

CS5-22.note: Text 2 disputes the cause while conceding the fact ('Submission counts fall wherever the odds ... are visibly worse'), so the shared claim is the bare submission count. C is Text 2 only. Standard agreement item, found in one pass.

CS5-23.note: Two outcomes moving in opposite directions under one control: matched time erases the recall gap (so time, not motor rehearsal, explained that) while the reproduction gap survives (so motor rehearsal explains that one). C is the exact inversion and A and D each drop one half. The hardest of the paired-text items and the one that most rewards close reading.

CS5-24.note: Inversion holds. The water table is explicitly frozen and the pond count explicitly decoupled ('reaches with ponds gained no more height'), so both stock answers are dead; the June/August survey months against July growth, plus the same-month null, fix C. D is an invention. Good item.

CS5-05.verdict: The senses do not in fact cluster. Efficiency is killed in the text's own words ('neither is the quicker to work with'), Prosperity is the everyday sense with no foothold, Arrangement is a live but unsupported sense, and the closing sentence defines parsimony. The item's real cost is difficulty, not ambiguity: pre-empting Efficiency explicitly is what drops it from hard to medium. Ship as is.

CS5-07.verdict: Worse. Beyond the blind default, C (Discharged) is eliminable from the STEM alone — questions are not discharged — and A is killed by the opening clause, so the item collapses to B against a weak D with B also being the guesser's default. Graded easy and weak. This is the one item I would re-key or re-author: the passage is good enough to carry a non-default sense of 'settled' (e.g. keying the by-fiat/quieted reading) if the options were rebuilt around it.

CS5-14.verdict: Worse: two rejectable options, not one. A is self-contradictory (the western pattern explained by eastern raiding) and C contradicts the passage's final clause. Only the stock null option B stands between the solver and the key. Easy.

CS5-16.verdict: Worse: the rejectable option is rejectable WITHOUT the passage. Three options open 'help readers' and A opens 'cost the psalm', an odd-one-out split, and B and C invent content with no textual hook while the key paraphrases a clause verbatim. Easy and weak.

CS5-20.verdict: The flag is too harsh. D is unsupported but not rejectable without reading Text 2, and A and C are both live stock answers defused only by explicit clauses. This is the strongest of the four flagged items; no change needed.

additional_item_the_author_did_not_flag.issue: The only second_defensible in my grade. With 'the diarist's account' as the subject, D (Indicate) reads naturally as the show/betray sense and is supported by the flat-syntax evidence and by 'Grief enters the diary only four months later'. I pick B, but D survives on the passage as written. Repair before insert: make the diarist the subject, or add a clause that closes the display sense.

template_groups.answer: No option-shape template exceeds four items, but one RHETORICAL template covers five, and a distractor-construction signature recurs across three.

groups.name: Word-in-context completion (blank, 'most logical and precise')
groups.note: At the limit but internally varied: 01 uses an appositive gloss, 02 a since-clause, 03 two stated traps, 04 a double inversion.

groups.name: 'As used in the text, X most nearly means'
groups.note: Three of the four (05, 06, 08) work by explicitly pre-empting the obvious sense with a 'not spare' / 'neither is the quicker' style clause. That is itself a mild authoring signature: a solver who learns to look for the sentence that negates a sense finds the key without weighing the options.

groups.name: Function of a named sentence
groups.note: All four use the parallel-stem, varying-tail option shape. Fine, but it is four in a row.

groups.name: Overall structure ('describes X ... and ends by Y')
OVER THRESHOLD: Text 2 undercuts Text 1's causal claim by naming a confound
groups.note: Five of the six paired-text items run the identical move; only CS5-22 (agreement) breaks it. A solver reaching item 21 knows the shape of the answer before reading the options. Consider replacing one with a strengthening pair, a disagreement-about-interpretation pair, or a Text-2-extends-Text-1 pair.

groups.name: Distractor signature: Text 2 pre-negates the wrong answers, so the key is the one variable it does NOT freeze
groups.note: Under the four threshold but the more dangerous pattern, and it is exactly the inversion the repair introduced. CS5-19 freezes night staffing, CS5-20 freezes nitrogen and weeds, CS5-24 freezes the water table and the pond effect. In all three the key is reachable by scanning Text 2 for the clause that is stated WITHOUT a neutralising 'unchanged / the same / no more' — the solver never has to reason about the mechanism. The inversion works against subject knowledge, as intended, but it installs a new cross-item tell. Vary it: on at least one item let a neutralised variable be irrelevant rather than a distractor, or leave a distractor un-neutralised and beaten on other grounds.
